49949680.article_summary: 文章介绍了 Rust 的 `#[derive]` 实现（如 `Debug`、`Clone`）目前会自动添加 `#[inline]`。这通常有利于优化，但复杂、嵌套的错误类型会导致大量代码被重复内联，显著增大二进制体积。作者发现 uv 因此可减少约 160KB，并通过自定义过程宏使用 `#[inline(never)]` 避免该问题。
49949680.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Rust 中 `Debug`/`Display` 实现的内联策略，讨论性能、二进制体积、编译时间与优化准确性之间的权衡。

不同观点：
• **尽量延迟或避免生成 `Debug`**：vlovich123认为，绝大多数 `Debug` 实现并不会被使用，理想方案是首次使用时才展开，仅保留特殊标记；但承认实现难度极高。其还指出，相关性能改进 PR 同时包含收益与回退，效果并不纯粹。  
• **默认不内联格式化实现**：Sharlin认为 `Debug` 甚至 `Display` 都不应内联，因为格式化机制本身较重，内联未必是瓶颈；他通过给自定义实现加 `#[inline(never)]`，将二进制缩小了数十 KB。  
• **采用表驱动方案**：scottlamb提议参考 `facet`，用表格描述 `derive(Debug)`，以优先降低二进制大小和编译时间；但也指出 `facet` 目前未完全证明该方案的效果，标准库可能已尝试并放弃。  
• **依靠 PGO 自动决策**：zamazan4ik建议使用基于实际运行数据的 PGO，动态决定哪些函数内联。api补充说 LLVM 通常激进内联，可用 `-Os/-Oz` 或 `#[inline(never)]` 控制，但过度抑制内联会损害性能。

补充讨论：争议焦点是默认内联究竟应优先追求运行速度，还是应牺牲部分速度以减少代码膨胀；普遍观点认为没有适用于所有程序的固定策略，PGO可能更可靠。

Trigora
Durable execution without history replay.
Trigora is a durable execution platform for long-lived AI agents and programs.
Write normal application logic in
TypeScript, Python, or Rust
. Trigora can suspend execution across events, timers, external effects, and child programs, then recover from committed continuation state after failure without replaying completed execution history.

"approved"

Deploy it once. Start executions from the CLI, an API call, a webhook, or a cron trigger. Let them run for seconds, hours, or days.
Why Trigora?
Traditional durable workflow systems often reconstruct execution state by replaying prior history.
Trigora uses
Transparent Continuation Checkpointing (TCC)
instead.
At durable boundaries, TCC commits the program position and the live durable state required to continue. Recovery resumes from that committed continuation rather than re-executing the completed prefix.
That makes Trigora a natural fit for workloads that:
run long-lived AI agents;
call models, tools, APIs, and external systems;
wait for humans or external events;
sleep for minutes, hours, or days;
coordinate durable child executions;
branch dynamically;
need to survive worker or process failure.
How TCC works →
Read the technical report →
Start building
Install the SDK, client, and CLI for your language.
TypeScript
npm install @trigora/sdk @trigora/client trigora
Python
pip install trigora trigora-client trigora-cli
Requires Python 3.10–3.14.
Rust
cargo add trigora trigora-client
cargo install trigora-cli
Then initialize a project:
trigora init
Start the local runtime:
trigora dev
When you're ready to run in production:
trigora deploy
Read the quickstart →
Trigora Cloud
Trigora Cloud
is the managed production runtime for TCC programs.
It provides:
durable execution;
deployment and program versioning;
events and timers;
cron and webhook triggers;
project secrets;
execution inspection and observability;
workspace access and API tokens;
managed persistence and recovery.
Start at
cloud.trigora.dev
.

Repository

This repository

contains the pieces shared across the Trigora ecosystem:

trigora

Language-specific authoring APIs live in their respective repositories above.
TCC Engine
TCC Engine
is the portable execution technology underneath Trigora.
It is implemented primarily in Rust, supports native and WebAssembly embedding, and has declared frontends for TypeScript, Python, and Rust.
The engine is available separately for teams that want to embed TCC into their own runtimes or infrastructure.
TCC Engine on GitHub →
TCC Engine is source-available under the Business Source License 1.1 and converts to Apache 2.0 under its license terms. The Trigora SDKs, clients, CLI, and public contracts are MIT licensed.
Research
The public research covers:
continuation-based recovery;
matched recovery versus history replay;
live-state scaling;
crash recovery and fresh-process restore;
frontend semantics;
host responsibilities;
limitations and failure windows.

data.title: Show HN: Procinsh – A 3D Linux process inspector
data.author: a_kawashiro
data.article_summary: ProcInSh 是一款面向 Linux 的网页进程检查器，可浏览进程空间，查看进程内存和环境变量。项目支持通过 crates.io 安装或源码编译，依赖 Rust、C/Clang、BPF 工具及相关开发库，运行后访问本地 9090 端口。支持远程访问，但无身份认证，存在敏感信息泄露风险；WSL2 支持有限。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：procinsh 将 Linux 进程、资源与通信关系以实时3D界面呈现，兼具系统监控工具与科幻/游戏化体验。

不同观点：
• 作者介绍其功能与实现：展示进程活动、内存映射、文件 I/O 和 Socket 通信；后端使用 Rust、procfs、eBPF、ptrace、process_vm_readv。  
• 多数评论认可其视觉效果，认为像黑客题材影视作品，具有很强的沉浸感和展示性；也有人调侃可借此向非技术亲友炫耀，并查看大量 tmux/Claude Code 进程。  
• 有评论将其与历史项目 psDoom、另一款“把进程做成怪物并通过击杀发送 kill 信号”的工具联系起来，强调“游戏化进程管理”的传统与趣味。  
• 技术角度的讨论指出，抓取 procfs 时需处理进程在读取过程中瞬间退出、PID消失等竞态问题，这可能是实现中的难点。  
• 有人从性能和自指问题调侃：procinsh 本身也需要另一个监控器来监视，暗示3D渲染可能带来较高资源开销。

补充讨论：评论整体偏正面和幽默，没有明显立场冲突；潜在争议集中在工具的实用性、性能开销，以及“杀死 init 等关键进程”可能导致系统崩溃的风险。

不同观点：
• **质疑基准测试有效性**：测试要求模型根据压缩文本回答固定问题，并采用严格的精确匹配；即使答案客观正确、只是措辞不同，也会被判错。纯文本基线也仅约91%，说明评分器偏好实现者的特定表述，不能据此证明压缩表达具有“涌现优势”。  
• **认为这可能已被实际系统采用**：有评论者从ChatGPT偶尔泄露的推理/UI内容推测，近期所谓“减少token”可能已经通过提示模型使用电报体实现；OpenAI智能体之间的通信也被认为出现过类似形式。  
• **批评其语言质量**：LLM常把抽象概念说成“物体会占据、承载、坐在某处”，并用低信息量、模糊词替代更准确的描述，被批评为“偷懒”或AI写作腔；有人建议提示“减少歧义”。  
• **认为简化语言有潜在价值**：电报体类似历史商业密码，能以短代码传递复杂信息；也有人主张人类写作本身应更简洁，如“简单维基”或规范化表达。  
• **怀疑其实际意义**：有人将其讽刺为“AI版穴居人语言”，认为让模型模仿特定口吻就能提升基准分，属于不严肃的技术炒作。

补充讨论：评论还提到历史商业电报码、Churchill式电报笑话、短信时代语言，以及AI配图和文章本身充满“AI垃圾”的问题。争议焦点在于：压缩通信究竟是有效工程优化，还是迎合评分器与模型写作缺陷。

Everything below is reproducible — harness, frozen ledgers, one-click notebook:
github.com/Travis42/telegraph-test
.
The Telegraph era, where every word was metered
#
In 1866, sending a message across the new transatlantic cable cost
$100 — for ten words
1
$10 a word, ten-word minimum,
roughly $2,600 in today’s money
.
. That’s real money today; it was serious money then. Telegraph companies charged
per word
, and an entire industry grew out of that price structure.
The Great Eastern laying the first successful Atlantic cable (oil painting, National Maritime Museum, public domain). The link that charged $10 a word — and taught a generation of correspondents to write in cablese.
Two compression strategies emerged, and they map onto two very different technologies:
Codebooks.
Publishers sold massive commercial code dictionaries — Bentley’s ABC Telegraphic Code ran to a thousand pages mapping entire business phrases to single code words.
OTTER
…might mean
*steamship arrived, cargo intact, remit balance.*
Firms could cut a 40-word negotiation to a 6-word coded exchange. The codebook is a
substitution
technology: the message exists in full prose, and a dictionary renames chunks of it.
Cablese.
The operators and correspondents evolved a written format like:
"ARRIVE TUESDAY BRING FUNDS STOP CONFIRM WIFE SAILS FRIDAY."
This disciplined style saved words without losing meaning, and it was emergent from the cost of the medium.
Over time, this format faded as new technologies like the telephone, fax, email, made the per-word cost premium collapse. Telegraphese kind of survives wherever metering in terms of cost or just the time it takes to tap out a message is still onerous: 160-character SMS begat a whole new abbreviation culture; early Twitter did it again.
Well guess what?
Tokens are metered words again
#
An LLM API bill is a telegraph bill. You pay per token.
So we ran both strategies from ye olden days against modern models:
The Codebook: take existing text, substitute code words from a fixed dictionary.
#
Result: about 10% savings. Most prose isn’t dictionary-shaped, and the substitution can’t remove words the author already wrote — it can only rename them.
Cablese
#
Instruct the model, “Write a complete record in telegraphese; drop articles and filler; abbreviate; keep every fact, number, and proper noun verbatim — in lowercase, not all caps.”
Numbers from a 50-passage, ~1,300-question benchmark:
Cross-family matrix
(readers = foreign models answering from GLM-5.3-Flash’s records; writers = GLM-5.3-Flash answering from theirs)
2
Savings shown use the lowercase instruction, on each provider’s own meter. Without that word, models write cablese in ALL CAPS and the styling costs 14–19 points: gemma 25.0%, qwen 29.8%, GLM 33.9%. *gpt-5-mini cannot disable reasoning, and compression makes it think — its writes bill about double plain. data.title: Strands Decider 2B: a small, open-source, decision model
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 文章介绍 Strands Decider 2B，一款面向智能体工作流的开源决策模型。它舍弃文本生成能力，专注于从给定选项中快速选择并提供可靠性评分，适合本地低延迟运行，但不擅长复杂推理、聊天和写作。该模型基于 Qwen3.5-2B，约20亿参数，可在 CPU/GPU 上运行，延迟约115毫秒，准确率和校准能力表现突出。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：决策模型的性能、适用场景、运行部署及架构机制。

不同观点：
• **部署与效率**：real_faxenoff认为模型长期在CPU后台运行体验不佳，应卸载到NPU；NPU性能可约提升一倍、功耗降至四分之一且更安静，并计划制作NPU/iGPU方案。teruakohatu则关心CPU运行效果。  
• **实际用途与评价**：miguelspizza已在浏览器扩展中用于邮件过滤，认为其兼顾体积、能力和速度，适合批量分类；CMay认为它适合快速、原子化决策，可通过链式调用完成复杂任务，但不擅长真正推理。dev_l1x_be报告PDF分类效果不稳定，Jev更好。  
• **基准争议**：ricardobeat批评JevBench过度偏重文本分类，不能代表实际智能能力；gsnedders质疑为何v10/v11被列为“其他系统”，且v11胜过v19却未被采用。  
• **生态与兼容性**：hrpnk担忧依赖Strands CLI会限制普及，希望支持llama.cpp；当前LoRA转GGUF存在报错。woadwarrior01补充Intern-Decision系列采用Qwen基础模型和pointer head。  
• **机制与扩展**：mynti询问多token选项如何由pointer head评分；SubiculumCode期待支持多模态及概率化判断；girvo关注针对特定问题微调是否优于通用模型。  
• **其他讨论**：有人质疑“noul”命名是否只是沿用Jev API，也有人以“真人Jerry”讽刺人工决策模型。

补充讨论：总体争议集中在基准是否能反映真实能力、决策模型与普通LLM的边界，以及部署生态是否成熟。

49987076.article_content:
Earlier this year, we announced
strands-labs
, a place to get hands-on with state-of-the-art approaches to agentic AI. Today, we’re excited to add Strands Decider 2B: a small decision model optimized for fast experimentation, local development, and innovation.
Strands decider is one of a new class of decision models or system one models, a type of model that has been gaining a lot of attention since TypeSafe AI’s launch of Jev earlier this month. Unlike LLMs that can generate arbitrary output, decision models are designed to pick between sets of options (e.g. “Is the string ‘turn on the lights’ about the coffee machine? Yes or no.”, “What language is the phrase ‘sihamba ngokushesha’ in? English, Zulu, or Dutch.”) and assign simple numerical scores (e.g. “Is the phrase ‘this is the best doc I’ve ever read’ a positive sentiment? Between 0 and 1.”).
In exchange for this reduction in flexibility, decision models are faster and more capable at a given size, always produce an answer from the selected options, and can run with very low latency.
The flip side is that this approach (generating all outputs in a single parallel pass) makes it significantly worse at solving complex problems than reasoning models, and its lack of ability to generate text makes it unsuited for coding, chatbots, document summarization, and other common LLM tasks.
In addition, decision models give each decision a high-quality reliability score (i.e. “how sure can I be that this yes/no is correct?”), which is not available through frontier LLM inference APIs. They also make it highly efficient to ask multiple questions about the same prompt. This combination of properties makes them perfect for driving the types of agentic workflows we see many developers building with the Strands Harness SDK, and the recently launched Strands harness. We expect that this class of model is going to lead to a lot of interesting innovation in agentic AI over the next few weeks, months, and years.
Strands Decider 2B is our first contribution to that innovation. It’s a 2 billion parameter model, suitable for running on a local CPU or GPU, which can return answers to meaningful questions in tens of milliseconds. Its accuracy and calibration is competitive with the other models we know of in this class. We’ve released
strands-decider-2b
as open source on
GitHub
, with the weights on
Hugging Face
, including all the training data and scripts we used to build the model, making it a great place to start on your own innovation journey.
Model Architecture
The core idea is that we take a pre-trained LLM torso (Qwen3.5-2B), and remove the LM head, taking away its ability to generate text. The LM head is replaced with a pointer head which scores the answers offered by the torso for each option. It does this by scoring the hidden state at each option position against the hidden state at the
<answer>
position. This head is pretty small, just over a million total parameters. The torso is fine-tuned with a rank-16 LoRA adapter.
Figure 1: The Strands Decider 2B architecture.
As you browse through the repo, you’ll find that this is the second major iteration of the architecture. The first one was similar, but used a slot head that we found performed significantly worse. In fact, the model we’re releasing today is v19, with lots of iterations under the covers. Everything we changed in each version is covered in the repo, and you can follow along with the work we did.
How does it perform?
For models of this type, we’re interested in three performance targets: accuracy (how well it answers questions), calibration (how trustworthy its confidence scores are), and latency (how quickly it can make decisions). We’ve been measuring the first two together: accuracy on JevBench’s public set, and calibration using the Brier score on the same set. We’ve found that
strands-decider-2b
performs well on accuracy and calibration (
3rd of 33 in the 2B class, and 1st of 30 excluding the just-over-2B models
). As we’ve evolved the architecture our scores are getting better, and we have many ideas for future improvements. We hope the community joins us, in the spirit of Strands labs, in contributing new ideas of your own.
Figure 2: Accuracy and calibration (Brier score) across the training trajectory. As the architecture evolved over successive versions, both metrics improved on JevBench’s public set.
On latency,
strands-decider-2b
can make local decisions in a median of around 115ms on widely available hardware. The time taken to decide depends on the task size, approximately linearly increasing as the task size gets larger. The results in the graph here are on a local Nvidia RTX3090, but the performance on an M3 MacBook isn’t much worse, with a median latency for small tasks around 153ms. As with accuracy and calibration, we have a lot of ideas for getting better here, especially in reducing the floor.
Figure 3: Decision latency as a function of task size (in tokens), measured on a local Nvidia R

data.title: Show HN: AstroHelm – Use your phone camera to aim a telescope or telephoto lens
data.author: HeavenFox
data.article_summary: AstroHelm是一款将手机安装在望远镜或相机上的天文导航应用，通过实时星图匹配（plate solving）精准判断指向，指导用户寻找星系、星云、行星和恒星。它无需GoTo设备、专业天文知识或网络，适用于多种器材，并支持离线运行及连接Stellarium、SkySafari等软件。基础功能免费，完整星表和远程控制等功能需一次性付费升级。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AstroHelm 将离线板块解算（plate solving）引入智能手机，用于望远镜定位、天文导航和非智能化设备。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为无需额外硬件、完全离线，适合无网络的荒野、高山、沙漠等观星环境，也可替代 PiFinder；传统计算机视觉相比机器学习更省电、低延迟且结果稳定。  
• 用户希望增加极轴校准功能，认为这对星野追踪器和简易赤道仪尤为重要。  
• 有人质疑手机镜头与望远镜光学系统的距离、视场差异会影响解算精度；另有人担心老旧手机或夜空弱信号下的识别效果。  
• 产品宣称精度约10角秒、计算不到1秒，但评论指出天空每秒移动约15角秒；没有电动跟踪时，定位精度很快会失效。  
• 有人希望推出 Android “Plus”版本，也有人认为 Stardroid/SkyMap 等免费开源软件已能满足类似需求。

补充讨论：争议集中在目镜适配器支持上。应用称目镜视场通常过小、无法板块解算，但用户指出自己用5mm目镜时仍能成功找到目标，质疑产品说明可能过于绝对或存在矛盾。

Know exactly
where you’re pointing
Mount your smartphone on a telescope or camera.
AstroHelm
continuously plate-solves the sky to guide you directly to galaxies, nebulae, planets, and stars—or precisely frame them for photography. No GoTo mount or proprietary hardware required.
Free to use. No subscription.
Download_on_the_App_Store_Badge_US-UK_RGB_wht_092917
See mounting options →
New to astronomy?
See something incredible tonight
A telescope opens up the wonders of the night sky — but getting started
can be surprisingly difficult. What should you look at? How do you find
it? What if you don't know the constellations?
Personalized guide to the night sky
AstroHelm comes with a curated list of great objects to observe and
highlights the best ones for your location and time. From bright
planets to faint galaxies and nebulae, AstroHelm helps you find
what’s worth seeing.
Pick, follow, and discover
Choose an object and AstroHelm shows you which way to move your
telescope. Your phone’s camera recognizes the stars overhead and
continuously determines where your telescope is pointing with high
precision, ensuring the object lands right in your eyepiece.
No astronomy knowledge required
No need to learn star hopping or memorize constellations. And unlike
a GoTo mount, there’s no complicated multi-star alignment. Better
yet, AstroHelm can find its way even under heavily light-polluted
skies.
Live Plate Solving
Observatory-Grade Precision in Your Pocket
Traditional astronomy apps rely on your phone's compass and gyroscope,
which drifts and lags. AstroHelm takes a picture of the night sky and
matches it against a massive database of stars, so it always knows
where you are pointing.
Accurate up to within 10 arcseconds (1/360 of a degree)
Computes coordinates in less than a second
Immune to magnetic field interference
Works even in the most light polluted cities
Features
Everything you need under the stars
Casual stargazers, serious amateur astronomers, and aspiring astrophotographers. AstroHelm is for everyone.
Precision Navigation
Standard planetarium apps have pointing errors of several degrees, putting objects out of view. AstroHelm matches real stars in the sky to pinpoint your exact coordinates with sub-arcminute accuracy.
Works Offline
The best dark-sky sites don't have Internet access. AstroHelm’s plate solving engine runs entirely on device. No internet connection required, and your camera images stay on your phone.
Hardware Agnostic
AstroHelm works with equipment you already have, whether it's a dobsonian, a DIY telescope, or a telephoto lens. No lock-in. No proprietary hardware.
Find Tonight’s Highlights
Not sure what to observe? Discover rewarding targets for your location and tonight’s sky, taking altitude, twilight, and moonlight into consideration.
Keep the Sky in Your Hands
Leave one device on your telescope and guide it from another in your hand, so you can explore the sky without reaching for the mounted screen.
Connect Your Favorite Apps
Works with astronomy software you already use, including Stellarium and SkySafari. AstroHelm acts as a telescope through ASCOM Alpaca, INDI, or LX200.
What Astronomers Are Saying
“After that, whatever I called for was in the field of view, even when I was using a 5mm eyepiece.”
— CloudyNights member
“I’m really impressed… guided me almost dead on to the double cluster when asked.”
— Stargazers Lounge member
“This app has been so good that I sold my other push-to and GoTo hardware.”

49954015.article_summary: AstroHelm是一款将手机安装在望远镜或相机上的天文导航应用，通过实时星图匹配（plate solving）精准判断指向，指导用户寻找星系、星云、行星和恒星。它无需GoTo设备、专业天文知识或网络，适用于多种器材，并支持离线运行及连接Stellarium、SkySafari等软件。基础功能免费，完整星表和远程控制等功能需一次性付费升级。
49954015.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AstroHelm 将离线板块解算（plate solving）引入智能手机，用于望远镜定位、天文导航和非智能化设备。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为无需额外硬件、完全离线，适合无网络的荒野、高山、沙漠等观星环境，也可替代 PiFinder；传统计算机视觉相比机器学习更省电、低延迟且结果稳定。  
• 用户希望增加极轴校准功能，认为这对星野追踪器和简易赤道仪尤为重要。  
• 有人质疑手机镜头与望远镜光学系统的距离、视场差异会影响解算精度；另有人担心老旧手机或夜空弱信号下的识别效果。  
• 产品宣称精度约10角秒、计算不到1秒，但评论指出天空每秒移动约15角秒；没有电动跟踪时，定位精度很快会失效。  
• 有人希望推出 Android “Plus”版本，也有人认为 Stardroid/SkyMap 等免费开源软件已能满足类似需求。

补充讨论：争议集中在目镜适配器支持上。应用称目镜视场通常过小、无法板块解算，但用户指出自己用5mm目镜时仍能成功找到目标，质疑产品说明可能过于绝对或存在矛盾。

data.title: How did Rosalind Franklin miss the helix in her iconic DNA image? She didn't
data.author: pavel_lishin
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕罗莎琳德·富兰克林是否在沃森和克里克之前认识到DNA的双螺旋结构，以及她与“照片51”、碱基互补和反平行结构的具体贡献展开争论。

不同观点：
• **富兰克林可能较早认识到双螺旋**：有评论者认为她的笔记显示，她已提出双螺旋及中心的碱基互补关系；但是否认识到两条链反平行，证据仍不足。  
• **富兰克林的重要贡献不等于完成最终模型**：她和威尔金斯通过X射线衍射，尤其是“照片51”，提供了B-DNA为螺旋结构的关键证据。但其笔记和相关证据多属间接，尚不能证明她独立、完整地得出了双螺旋模型。  
• **沃森和克里克完成了分子模型**：支持者认为，双螺旋并非仅凭照片即可直接推出，链数、碱基配对和反平行排列仍是开放问题；沃森和克里克在1953年首次构建了成功的双螺旋模型。  
• **反对“单一英雄/单一突破”叙事**：DNA结构发现经历多年合作、竞争和排除错误模型的过程，富兰克林、威尔金斯、沃森和克里克分别在螺旋证据、成像、模型和复制机制等方面作出贡献。诺奖未授予富兰克林，主要因她去世较早。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“发现DNA结构”应指发现螺旋、双螺旋，还是完整的碱基配对与反平行模型；另有评论批评标题夸张、将复杂的集体发现简化为富兰克林与沃森之间的归属之争。

data.title: GPT‑6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
data.author: joshuawright11
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPT-6引入“视觉与交互式解释”、智能UI及其在ChatGPT中的应用，同时引发对实用性、设计、模型选择和安全性的争议。

不同观点：
• 支持创新者认为，交互式解释能让抽象概念“活起来”，类似 Mathematica 的 Manipulate，是聊天界面走向更丰富交互的第一步；自动生成小众主题的互动解释尤其令人惊叹。  
• 反对过度UI者担心“纸盘式/一次性UI”喧宾夺主：用户有时只想要简短答案，却被迫浏览卡片、标题和大量留白；若误触发或答非所问，会妨碍交流。  
• 设计批评者认为GPT-6过度使用标签、分栏、装饰间距和卡片，显得居高临下、像对待儿童，担心这种风格渗透到工作工具。另有人指出其视频播放器本身体验很差。  
• 模型与质量方面，有人质疑ChatGPT采用GPT-6而非能力更强的6.1；视觉解释虽有潜力，但模型可靠性仍不足。  
• 安全质疑者指出系统卡显示自残、血腥、色情及极端主义评测出现显著退步，却仍以“闪亮UI”作为宣传重点。  
• 其他担忧包括UI可能成为广告入口、把过多产品塞进ChatGPT，以及闭源商业模式；有人要求开放权重和模型信息。

补充讨论：用户更偏好逐句追问式学习，担心模型反复生成无关可视化；核心争议是创新交互与简洁、准确、安全之间如何取舍。

data.title: Margaret Hamilton has died
data.author: muglug
data.article_summary: 计算机科学先驱玛格丽特·汉密尔顿于9月30日去世，享年90岁。她曾在MIT领导阿波罗计划软件开发团队，为登月任务成功提供关键代码，并推动“软件工程”成为独立学科。她还创办计算机企业，获得包括2016年美国总统自由勋章在内的多项荣誉。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕玛格丽特·汉密尔顿逝世展开悼念，并讨论她在阿波罗计划、软件工程和早期计算机领域的贡献及历史评价。

不同观点：
• 多数评论高度赞誉她是杰出的软件先驱，尤其因阿波罗项目贡献、复杂控制系统工作，以及“software engineer”（软件工程师）一词而闻名；她借此推动软件获得与硬件同等的工程地位。  
• 许多人通过她抱着代码打印稿的标志性照片认识她，认为这张照片象征其传奇经历；也有人提到计算机历史博物馆的口述史、阿波罗展览和相关科普视频。  
• 有人分享亲历或间接接触：曾与MIT仪器实验室/德雷珀实验室成员交流，称她谈论的形式化控制系统令人震撼但深奥；另有评论推测她可能参与过TX-0上的天气模拟程序。  
• 少数评论对主流叙述提出质疑，指出有基于一手资料的文章认为她实际参与登月项目的程度被夸大，其知名度上升也与“寻找被忽视的科学英雄”的维基百科行动有关。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于如何准确界定她在阿波罗登月项目中的具体贡献，而非否定其软件工程先驱地位。整体评论以悼念、敬佩和传播史料为主。

Margaret Hamilton, a profoundly influential computer scientist best known for leading the software engineering team at MIT’s Instrumentation Lab during NASA’s Apollo program, died on Sep. 30. She was 90.
A computing pioneer who authored over 130 publications, Hamilton helped to establish software engineering as a dedicated discipline. She worked at MIT from 1959 until the mid-1970s, after which she became a successful computing entrepreneur and CEO.
Her life’s work was recognized with many awards and honors,
including the 2016 Presidential Medal of Freedom
from President Barack Obama, whose citation noted: “Hamilton defined new forms of software engineering and helped launch an industry that would forever change human history. Her software architecture led to giant leaps for humankind, writing the code that helped America set foot on the moon.”
“To say Margaret Hamilton was a pioneer — to say she was ahead of her time — would be a dramatic understatement. She was a software engineer at a time when that field was in its infancy, and she not only developed advanced code herself but also led a team in using that nascent technology to develop one of the most complex systems humanity had ever achieved,” says Olivier de Weck, the Apollo Program Professor and interim head of the MIT Department Aeronautics and Astronautics.
“The Apollo program still stands as one of our greatest testaments to the power of collaboration, ingenuity, and engineering, and Margaret Hamilton was a fundamental contributor to that program’s success. And for her that was just the beginning! She went on to become an entrepreneur and remained on the cutting edge of systems software throughout an extraordinary career, while acting as an advocate, mentor, and inspiration to millions.”
Early life and projects at MIT
Born in Paoli, Indiana, in 1936, Hamilton began studying mathematics at the University of Michigan in 1955 before transferring to Earlham College, where she earned a BA in mathematics with a minor in philosophy in 1958. She moved to Boston, Massachusetts, in 1959 with her husband while he pursued a law degree.
Hamilton soon found a temporary position in the meteorology department at MIT, working with professor of meteorology Edward N. Lorenz SM ’43, ScD ’48 on weather prediction software. This was her first entry point into computer programming, and her work would go on to inform Lorenz’s future publications on chaos theory.
From there, Hamilton took a role as a programmer at MIT Lincoln Laboratory in 1961, working on the
Semi-Automatic Ground Environment

data.title: Claude Haiku 5.5
data.author: sfkgtbor
data.article_summary: Anthropic发布Claude Haiku 5.5，定位为高速、低成本且能力更强的小型模型，适合摘要、分类、数据库查询、客服、浏览器操作及编码子代理等高频任务。其运行成本较Haiku 4.5平均降低约75%，并支持可调推理强度。与此同时，Sonnet 5.5缓存读取价格减半，Max和Team用户新增月度API额度。早期客户反馈其速度、准确率和代理任务表现显著提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Claude Haiku 5.5 的性能、价格、速度及适用场景，与 Luna、Sonnet/Opus 等模型的比较。

不同观点：
• 性价比显著提升：多数评论认为其较 Haiku 4.5 便宜约90%，速度快，适合分类、数据分析、小型代理任务；部分测试显示性能优于4.5，接近甚至超过 Luna，可能成为工作流替代品。  
• 价格仍有争议：10万 tokens 是较低的阶梯门槛，Agent 或长上下文任务容易触发更高价格；但短任务仍很便宜，且总体远低于4.5。有人指出 Luna 在长上下文下仍更便宜。  
• 能力评价不一：数据分析测试显示便宜且大体准确，但深层统计分析、复杂 UI 和持续推理较弱；有测试称其能识别自身不足并转交 Opus。也有人反馈实际使用中出现提示泄漏、结果糟糕且比4.5慢。  
• 与其他模型的定位：Luna 可能更便宜，Sonnet 5.5 在部分任务上已足够好；Opus 更适合复杂实现。Haiku 5.5 的优势主要是低价、低延迟和窄任务处理。  
• 订阅权益受欢迎：Max/Team 每月 API credits 被认为是重大福利，可将 Claude 额度用于外部工具和产品功能；但有人担心这是为缓解不友好的套餐变化。

补充讨论：评论还涉及图像转 HTML、SVG 生成、游戏反编译等实际案例，以及持续改进速度和 LLM 基准测试项目。

October 7, 2026
Claude
Haiku 5.5
Skip intro
Scroll down
Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5: the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we’ve ever released.
Claude Haiku 5.5 is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks. It reliably handles quick and repetitive workloads (like summaries, compactions, database queries, and classification requests). It pairs well with Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 as a subagent on coding work. And, since it’s also our fastest model to date, it works especially well for speed-sensitive tasks like live customer support and browser use.¹
Haiku 5.5 is available at a much lower price than Haiku 4.5. On average, it now costs around 75% less to run.²

49996437.article_summary: Anthropic发布Claude Haiku 5.5，定位为高速、低成本且能力更强的小型模型，适合摘要、分类、数据库查询、客服、浏览器操作及编码子代理等高频任务。其运行成本较Haiku 4.5平均降低约75%，并支持可调推理强度。与此同时，Sonnet 5.5缓存读取价格减半，Max和Team用户新增月度API额度。早期客户反馈其速度、准确率和代理任务表现显著提升。
49996437.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Claude Haiku 5.5 的性能、价格、速度及适用场景，与 Luna、Sonnet/Opus 等模型的比较。

不同观点：
• 性价比显著提升：多数评论认为其较 Haiku 4.5 便宜约90%，速度快，适合分类、数据分析、小型代理任务；部分测试显示性能优于4.5，接近甚至超过 Luna，可能成为工作流替代品。  
• 价格仍有争议：10万 tokens 是较低的阶梯门槛，Agent 或长上下文任务容易触发更高价格；但短任务仍很便宜，且总体远低于4.5。有人指出 Luna 在长上下文下仍更便宜。  
• 能力评价不一：数据分析测试显示便宜且大体准确，但深层统计分析、复杂 UI 和持续推理较弱；有测试称其能识别自身不足并转交 Opus。也有人反馈实际使用中出现提示泄漏、结果糟糕且比4.5慢。  
• 与其他模型的定位：Luna 可能更便宜，Sonnet 5.5 在部分任务上已足够好；Opus 更适合复杂实现。Haiku 5.5 的优势主要是低价、低延迟和窄任务处理。  
• 订阅权益受欢迎：Max/Team 每月 API credits 被认为是重大福利，可将 Claude 额度用于外部工具和产品功能；但有人担心这是为缓解不友好的套餐变化。

补充讨论：评论还涉及图像转 HTML、SVG 生成、游戏反编译等实际案例，以及持续改进速度和 LLM 基准测试项目。

data.article_summary: 文章介绍数学交流网站上的匿名用户“Cleo”。2013—2015年间，Cleo针对复杂积分题发布39个答案，解答迅速且准确，却几乎不展示推导，引发其身份与能力的讨论。其自称因健康问题难以交流，风格被比作拉马努金。2025年1月，Cleo身份被揭示为乌兹别克斯坦裔美国软件开发者兼数学家弗拉基米尔·列舍特尼科夫。

Vladimir Reshetnikov

integration
problems without showing any intermediate steps under the
pseudonym
Cleo

During the poster's active period, Cleo posted 39 answers to advanced mathematical questions, primarily focusing on complex
integration
problems that had stumped other users. Cleo's answers were characterized by being consistently correct while providing no explanation of methodology, often appearing within hours of the original posts. The account claimed to be limited in interaction due to an unspecified medical condition.
The mystery surrounding Cleo's identity and mathematical abilities generated interest within the mathematical community, and some users attempted to analyze solution patterns and writing style for clues. Some compared Cleo to historical mathematical figures like
Srinivasa Ramanujan
, who was known for providing solutions without conventional proofs. In January 2025, Cleo was revealed to be Vladimir Reshetnikov.

data.title: 'Jonathan' is the oldest land animal on Earth
data.author: gumby
data.article_summary: 科学家首次测序了194岁阿尔达布拉象龟“乔纳森”的基因组，并与其他龟类比较，发现其在DNA修复、端粒维护、胰岛素调节、线粒体功能和细胞自噬等衰老通路上拥有特殊变异。其线粒体相关甲基组异常“低熵”、近似幼年个体，或是长寿关键。研究仍处早期，未来可能为延长人类健康寿命提供线索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕长寿动物“Jonathan”及其衰老研究展开，涉及其基因特征、极端寿命、研究运输方式，以及人类是否应减少干扰。

不同观点：
• 科学解释派：研究称Jonathan在DNA修复、胰岛素调节、线粒体功能和“低熵”甲基化等多数衰老通路上具有独特基因变异，可能有助于解释其长寿。  
• 比较与质疑派：有人指出陆地动物寿命尚未普遍突破200年，而海洋生物可活到五六百年，借此质疑或拓展对“最长寿命”的理解；也有人调侃研究者“应该找年轻一点的”。  
• 保护、反干预立场：评论者认为应欣赏Jonathan的特殊性，不要过度研究或打扰这只动物。  
• 玩笑和文化联想：有人戏称其“看起来不超过90岁”、已经“分不清兔子”，也有人把圣赫勒拿岛比作《末日列车》（The Leftovers）中的Jarden，暗示其神秘性；另有“最大化寿命、牺牲速度和魅力”等戏谑表达。

补充讨论：美国太空军参与将样本从圣赫勒拿岛运往佛罗里达引发疑问，至少两条评论重复追问“为什么是太空军”，成为较集中的争议焦点；但评论中未提供明确解释。

The Abstract
‘Jonathan’ Is the Oldest Land Animal on Earth. He Could Hold the Secrets to Defying Death
Becky Ferreira
·
Oct 7, 2026
at 2:00 PM
Jonathan, a 194-year-old Aldabra giant tortoise, was born before the Civil War. Scientists have now sequenced his genome to reveal what’s behind his extreme longevity, so we can live longer too.
Jonathan, the world’s oldest living land animal, in the 1880s and today. Images: Wikimedia Commons and St. Helene Government, Communication Hub
Jonathan the tortoise, the world’s oldest living land animal, is still chugging along at the ripe age of roughly 194. Now, scientists have discovered some of the secrets to Jonathan’s longevity by sequencing his genome for the first time, according to
a study published Wednesday
in
Science Advances
.
Jonathan, a Aldabra giant tortoise (
Aldabrachelys gigantea
), hatched around 1832 in the Seychelles archipelago, and he was already in his twenties when Charles Darwin published
On the Origin of Species
. In his fifties, Jonathan was brought to the remote island of Saint Helena, along with three other tortoises, as a gift to the British colonial governor in the 1880s. He has lived there ever since.
Jonathan (left) in the 1880s. Image:
Wikipedia
Aldabra giant tortoises often become centenarians, but Jonathan is a major outlier even for his species as he approaches nearly 200 years on this planet. To better understand his extreme lifespan, researchers evaluated Jonathan’s genome based on swabs of his cheeks and compared it with the genomes of several other tortoises, including a 36-year-old named Tank.
The results revealed that Jonathan has “unique gene variants in most aging pathways” including DNA repair, insulin regulation, mitochondrial function, and “low entropy” methylation, reports the study.
“Aging is very complicated, and there's all these different hallmarks,” said Stephen Clark, an aging researcher at the
non-profit Kallel Foundation
and an author of the study, in a call with 404 Media. “That's why this Jonathan study is so interesting. We're still just at the very beginning of trying to understand aging.”
The study was not an easy lift. Clark first reached out to Jonathan’s caretakers in 2017, but it took some negotiating to figure out the best way to obtain the tortoise’s genetic information. A blood draw was deemed too risky, so Jonathan was coaxed into opening his mouth for a swab. The results were delayed by incomplete early samples, the Covid pandemic, and new regulations governing access to Jonathan.
🌘
Subscribe
to 404 Media to get
The Abstract
, our newsletter about the most exciting and mind-boggling science news and studies of the week.
After years of back and forth, the samples were delivered from Saint Helena to Florida by the U.S. Space Force. The results showed that Jonathan had many gene variants the team expected to see, based on studies of other long-lived individuals and populations. These included variants associated with DNA repair, maintenance of aging-related sequences called telomeres, and the process of cellular recycling known as autophagy.
But the researchers found a surprise in Jonathan’s “methylome,” which is a set of methyl-based modifications involved in gene expression. The subset of Jonathan’s methylome related to mitochondrial processes was unusually pristine, or “low entropy.”
Photo: St. Helene Government, Communication Hub
“Jonathan's really the first of his kind to have this analysis, and we were also able to do the methylome for the younger tortoises,” Clark said. “We actually compared him to a five-year-old tortoise, so we had 189 years of difference between the methylomes. No one's ever done that, even in humans, because no humans live that long. That was one of the main things we were excited about: how does this methylome change with age?”
Whereas most of Jonathan’s genome showed signs of entropy commensurate with his age, his mitochondrial methylome seemed on par with that of the five-year-old tortoise, signaling that these pathways may play a special role in his advanced age. However, Clark said it would take more research to follow up on that lead, and to untangle the complicated web of genetic components that influence aging and lifespan.
“We're interested in long-lived species like Jonathan because we can hopefully find other targets,” Clark said of his team’s work at Kallel Labs. “The ultimate goal of the company is to affect human healthspan and lifespan.”
As for Jonathan, he continues to live out his voluminous days at the governor’s residence, Plantation House, where he and his fellow tortoises have become one of the island’s tourist attractions. Saint Helena is also known for the exile of Napoleon Bonaparte, who died there a mere decade before Jonathan is thought to have been hatched. It’s amazing to think about just how much the world has changed in Jonathan’s lifetime. Long may he graze.

data.article_summary: 文章介绍作者用 Embedded Swift 编写并在 QEMU 的 ARM 裸机环境运行一个极简内核。项目通过开发版 Swift 工具链、汇编启动代码和自定义链接脚本，完成栈配置、入口跳转及输出消息。过程中解决了标准库缺失、链接器段配置以及 putchar、memmove 等运行库依赖问题，并说明可用新的 `@c` 属性替代实验性的 `@_cdecl`。

49977351.article_content:
Update (28th of September 2026)
Max Desiatov
told me
that
the
@c
swift attribute
should work, instead of declaring the functions using
@_cdecl
. The
@c
attribute marks a global function as a C function implemented in Swift, which formalizes the
@_cdecl
attribute. A link to the proposal is available
here
.
I did update the blog post and the code accordingly to that comment. Thanks Max!
I started a small experiment: writing a very basic kernel in Swift, and running on
QEMU
.
The goal is obviously not to replace Linux or any other popular kernel, but just to have fun and understand what is required to make a program run without an operating system underneath it.
Actually I made a similar experiment years before with
arOS
10 years ago.
For the moment, the kernel does only one thing: it prints a message through QEMU and then waits forever, which is enough for a first deep dive.
Swift Embedded
#
The project uses
Embedded Swift
, which is a subset of Swift designed for environments where there is no operating system and no standard library available (in the usual sense).
My first
Package.swift
was very small:
// swift-tools-version: 6.4
import
PackageDescription
let
package
= Package(
name:
"swift-kernel"
,
platforms: [.macOS(.v14)],
targets: [
.executableTarget(
name:
"swift_kernel"
,
swiftSettings: [
.enableExperimentalFeature(
"Embedded"
),
.strictMemorySafety(),
.treatAllWarnings(
as
: .error),
],
)
]
)
And the first Swift file was almost insulting in its simplicity:
// Sources/swift_kernel/test.swift
print
(
"Hello... world?"
)
I tried to run it:
> swift run
<unknown>:0: error: unable to load standard library
for
target
'arm64-apple-macosx27.0.0'
Oops.
It seems like my current Swift compiler does not yet ship with the Embedded Swift standard library.
As I missed in
the documentation
:
Since Embedded Swift is still experimental and not yet supported in public Swift releases, you’ll need to use a development toolchain.
So, let’s install the development toolchain and test again:
> swiftly install main-snapshot && swiftly use main-snapshot
> swift run
[...]
Hello... world?
Success!
At this point I had confirmed that Embedded Swift could compile and run a small program.
The next step was to compile for a machine with no operating system at all.
QEMU setup
#
For this project I will test on a machine emulator called
QEMU
, which is one of the most famous machine emulators for hackers.
I am using QEMU’s
virt
machine on an Apple Silicon machine. The target is therefore
aarch64-none-none-elf
.
This target, designed
as a triple
, describes a 64-bit ARM machine with no operating system and no environment provided by a C runtime.
When QEMU starts, the CPU is in a raw state.
Before it can safely execute Swift code, I need to
configure a stack
and
decide where the program starts
.
I will need a minimal assembly file that:
defines
the
_start
symbol
,
sets up a stack for the first core,
jumps to our Swift entry function,
kernel_main
,
and waits forever to keep the main running.
Compiler setup
#
I have to tell the compiler that this is not a normal executable: the compiler must avoid linking the usual standard libraries, and the linker must use our linker script instead of a platform-specific one.
The project uses the following
toolset.json
, which will be passed to our Swift Package Manager (SPM):
{
"schemaVersion":
"1.0"
,
"swiftCompiler": {
"extraCLIOptions": [
"-enable-experimental-feature"
,
"Embedded"
,
"-enable-experimental-feature"
,
"Volatile"
,
"-Xfrontend"
,
"-no-allocations"
,
"-Xfrontend"
,
"-function-sections"
,
"-Xfrontend"
,
"-disable-stack-protector"
,
"-Xlinker-driver"
,
"-nostdlib"
,
"-Xlinker-driver"
,
"-fuse-ld=lld"
]
},
"linker": {
"extraCLIOptions": [
"-nostdlib"
,
"-static"
,
"--gc-sections"
,
"--orphan-handling=error"
,
"-T"
,
"linker.ld"
,
"-Map"
,
".build/kernel.map"
]
}
}
Now, let’s build the project with the new target, the toolset, and Swift’s native build system:
> swift build --triple aarch64-none-none-elf --toolset toolset.json --build-system native
Unfortunately, the first linker attempt fails:
ld.lld: error: section type mismatch for .strtab
>>> <internal>:(.strtab): SHT_STRTAB
>>> output section .nonalloc: SHT_SYMTAB
ld.lld: error: section type mismatch for .shstrtab
>>> <internal>:(.shstrtab): SHT_STRTAB
>>> output section .nonalloc: SHT_PROGBITS
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: putchar
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: memmove
Hmm. What is going on here?
Because I am compiling for a bare-metal target (reminder:
none-none-elf
), there is no underlying operating system and no C standard library. Therefore there is no
putchar
, and there is no
memmove
either…
The section errors have a different origin.
With orphan handling enabled, the linker does not want to guess where ELF metadata should go. Therefore, the linker script must explicitly place the sections that I am keeping.
Bridging Swift to assembly
#
I can’t use a normal Swift file with a
main
function. Instead, I expose a designated kerne

data.title: Docker Agent
data.author: saikatsg
data.article_summary: Docker Agent 是 Docker 推出的 AI 智能体构建与运行工具，可通过 YAML 无代码定义智能体、工具及多智能体协作流程，并支持多种云端及本地模型。它提供丰富工具生态、RAG、记忆与任务管理能力，支持通过 CLI 运行、交互创建，以及以 OCI 镜像形式打包分享。项目采用 Apache-2.0 许可。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Docker Agent 的定位、价值、成熟度、安全边界，以及它与现有沙箱和代理框架的差异展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为，将代理编排直接纳入容器，有助于构建安全、可复现的开发流程；Docker Agent 也可能适合需要重复实验、验证结果的科研场景。  
• Olscore认为核心难题不是编排，而是代理长期运行中的“漂移”和一致性，提出用类似论坛的系统记录任务、共享信息，并通过开发者制定的规则和可检查规格约束代理。  
• 质疑者认为“无需代码”并非明显卖点，因为模型已经能快速生成大部分代码；先发布编排框架、却没有成熟代理，像是“本末倒置”。  
• 部分用户认为代理框架正在泛滥，像过去的 JavaScript 框架热潮；模型能力趋同后，各类 harness 主要是在寻找自身价值。  
• 有用户实际体验后认为 Docker Agent 过于脆弱，成熟度不足；也有人希望出现专门理解 Docker 的代理和模型，能一次性生成并部署高级配置。  
• 反对其必要性的观点指出，Modal、E2B、Cloudflare 等已有 Docker 结合运行与隔离方案，Docker Agent 的新增抽象不够清晰；另有人困惑它与 kagent、Agent Sandbox、LangChain、Cloudflare Sandboxes 的使用场景区别。

补充讨论：安全是重要争议点。评论者要求提供更明确的权限控制，包括命令 ACL、凭证限制、网络隔离及按 OAuth scope 动态申请权限；另有观点认为 uv 在跨平台、本地 GPU 实验和可复现环境方面已足够，Docker 并非总是最佳选择。

🤖 Docker Agent 🤖
Build, run, and share AI agents with a declarative YAML config, rich tool ecosystem, and multi-agent orchestration.
What is Docker Agent?
docker-agent
lets you create and run intelligent AI agents that collaborate to solve complex problems — no code required.
docker-agent
is a
docker
CLI plugin and can be run with
docker agent
.
Define agents in YAML, give them tools, and let them work.
agents
:
root
:
model
:
openai/gpt-5-mini
description
:
A helpful AI assistant
instruction
:
|
You are a knowledgeable assistant that helps users with various tasks.
Be helpful, accurate, and concise in your responses.
toolsets
:
-
type
:
mcp
ref
:
docker:duckduckgo
docker agent run agent.yaml
Key Features
Multi-agent architecture
— Create teams of specialized agents that delegate tasks automatically
Rich tool ecosystem
— Built-in tools + any
MCP
server (local, remote, or Docker-based)
AI provider agnostic
— OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Mistral, xAI,
Docker Model Runner
, and more
YAML configuration
— Declarative, versionable, shareable
Advanced reasoning
— Built-in think, todo, and memory tools
RAG
— Pluggable retrieval with BM25, embeddings, hybrid search, and reranking
Package & share
— Push agents to any OCI registry, pull and run them anywhere
Install
Docker Desktop
(4.63+) — docker-agent CLI plugin is pre-installed. Just run
docker agent
.
Homebrew
—
brew install docker-agent
. Run
docker-agent
directly or symlink the binary to
~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-agent
and run
docker agent
.
Binary releases
— Download from
GitHub Releases
. Symlink the
docker-agent
binary to
~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-agent
to be able to use
docker agent
, or use
docker-agent
directly.
Set at least one API key (or use
Docker Model Runner
for local models):
export
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
#
or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, etc.
See
Set Up a Model
for the full walkthrough of both paths (cloud API key or local model).
Quick Start
#
Run the default agent
docker agent run
#
Run from an OCI registry
docker agent run myorg/agent:tag
#
Generate a new agent interactively
docker agent new
#
Run your own config
docker agent run agent.yaml
More examples in the
examples/
directory.

data.title: Push ifs up and fors down: The idiom, its algebra, and its limits
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 文章介绍“把 if 往上推、把 for 往下压”的编程惯用法：由调用者集中处理分支，使辅助函数获得更明确的前置条件；将循环下沉到批处理函数，在过滤后进行无分支、高效迭代。该原则也对应数据库中提前投影、筛选、延后连接，以及向量化执行，并可从函数式编程和范畴论角度理解，同时讨论其适用边界。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：讨论“将条件判断移到循环外、让循环保持统一/无分支”这一代码结构建议，究竟应服务于可读性、可维护性，还是性能优化。

不同观点：
• 支持结构化拆分者认为，应把“分发数据”和“做判断”分开：先按类别分组，再对每组统一处理，使控制流更清晰、错误更显眼；也有人多年采用该方式，主要为了理解和维护，而非速度。  
• 性能导向者认为，无分支循环有利于分支预测、向量化及并行执行，在大规模、科学计算、GPU/集群场景尤其有效；但小规模程序通常无需关注。  
• 反对过度抽象者认为，应直接写普通的 `f(Walrus) -> Walrus`，由调用者处理空值或集合；专门为 `Collection<Optional<T>>` 设计抽象可能增加复杂度。  
• 工程折中观点认为，是否过滤、复制集合或并行化应以实际 profiling 和基准测试为依据；若性能不重要，应优先采用语言/框架中自然、常见的表达方式。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点是“性能收益是否被证明”以及是否值得牺牲代码直观性。有人指出现代 C#/C/C++ 编译器可能自动完成相关优化，文章却缺少基准和引用。  
• “提前判断”也被联系到 guard clause；另有观点提醒，深层拆分可能破坏不变量，最终仍可能演变成难维护的抽象或“为什么这个方法没被调用”的问题。

of TigerBeetle ..
Centralize control flow. When splitting a large function, try to keep all switch/if statements in the "parent" function, and move non-branchy logic fragments to helper functions. Divide responsibility. All control flow should be handled by one function, the rest shouldn't care about control flow at all. In other words, "push ifs up and fors down".
The programming heuristic push-ifs-up-fors-down suggests that conditional logic (if statements) should be moved upward (towards the caller or earlier in a pipeline), while iterative loops (for operations) should be pushed downward (toward batch processing or later in a tight branch-free loop). This improves clarity and performance by centralizing branching and leveraging bulk operations.
matklad has also
blogged
about this principle and discussed the many virtues of adhering to this programming idiom.
In the post, matklad describes optimizing code by:
Pushing conditionals ("ifs") up:
If a function branches on its input, consider moving that branch to the caller. Consider the example from the post - instead of
frobnicate(walrus: Option<Walrus>)
unpacking the option internally, the caller handles the
None
case and the function takes a plain
Walrus
. The function's type now states its precondition, the input state space becomes narrower and acts as a form of filtering. But the point is where the decision lives, not how much data flows downstream.
Pushing loops ("fors") down:
Deferring loops until after filtering or reducing the dataset minimizes unnecessary computations. Rather than calling
frobnicate(walrus)
in a loop, provide
frobnicate_batch(walruses)
and let the loop live inside it. So the hot loop runs without a branch and is a candidate for vectorization.
The two moves compose. Given a collection of
Option<Walrus>
values, the caller discards the
None
s and unwraps the rest into a
Vec<Walrus>
, then hands that to
frobnicate_batch
, which never has to consider the
None
case at all.

If you think a bit, the push-ifs-up-fors-down principle has far broader applications. This post explores some of the broader perspectives of this principle with respect to relational database query optimizations and functional programming and category theory.
Analogy in Database Queries: Projections Early, Joins Late
The same principle appears in database query optimization. In SQL query planning, it’s well-known that one should perform projections and selections as early as possible and defer joins or expansive operations until later. But the vocabulary runs upside-down. A query plan is a tree whose leaves are table scans and whose root produces the result. Data flows up from the leaves, so "down the tree" means "earlier in execution". When an optimizer talks about
pushing a predicate down
, it means evaluating it as early as possible, which is the database counterpart of what the rest of this post calls "up" or "early".
Early projections and selections (Push down):
In database terms, a projection (e.g., SELECT with specific columns) reduces the dataset's width by selecting only the necessary columns early in the query execution. And selections (WHERE clause) act as the filter. Both are pushed down as part of the plan tree so that they get to execute early and filter out irrelevant data, reducing the amount of data passed to later operations.
Deferring joins (Push joins up):
Joins, which combine data from multiple tables, are computationally expensive. The optimizer moves selections and projections below the joins, so joins run on smaller inputs. The effect is that the expensive combining operators run over the smallest inputs the query semantics allow.
Vectorized execution (the "for"):
Another database analogy of pushing fors down is the change in execution semantics. Volcano style execution processes row at a time, where each operator is called once per tuple through a virtual
next()
. The alternative is the vectorized or batch execution, where each operator is called once per batch of a thousand or so tuples and runs a tight loop inside. That is
frobnicate
versus
frobnicate_batch
, at the level of a query engine: the per-call overhead and the per-call decisions are paid once per batch, and the inner loop is branch-light and cache-friendly.
Analogy in Functional Programming and Category Theory
Let's take a look at the same principles through the lens of functional programming and category theory.
Pushing-Ifs-Up as a Restriction to a Subobject
In category theory, when we talk about the category of sets (or, loosely, of types in programming), we can have a predicate
49997073.article_summary: 文章介绍“把 if 往上推、把 for 往下压”的编程惯用法：由调用者集中处理分支，使辅助函数获得更明确的前置条件；将循环下沉到批处理函数，在过滤后进行无分支、高效迭代。该原则也对应数据库中提前投影、筛选、延后连接，以及向量化执行，并可从函数式编程和范畴论角度理解，同时讨论其适用边界。
49997073.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：讨论“将条件判断移到循环外、让循环保持统一/无分支”这一代码结构建议，究竟应服务于可读性、可维护性，还是性能优化。

不同观点：
• 支持结构化拆分者认为，应把“分发数据”和“做判断”分开：先按类别分组，再对每组统一处理，使控制流更清晰、错误更显眼；也有人多年采用该方式，主要为了理解和维护，而非速度。  
• 性能导向者认为，无分支循环有利于分支预测、向量化及并行执行，在大规模、科学计算、GPU/集群场景尤其有效；但小规模程序通常无需关注。  
• 反对过度抽象者认为，应直接写普通的 `f(Walrus) -> Walrus`，由调用者处理空值或集合；专门为 `Collection<Optional<T>>` 设计抽象可能增加复杂度。  
• 工程折中观点认为，是否过滤、复制集合或并行化应以实际 profiling 和基准测试为依据；若性能不重要，应优先采用语言/框架中自然、常见的表达方式。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点是“性能收益是否被证明”以及是否值得牺牲代码直观性。有人指出现代 C#/C/C++ 编译器可能自动完成相关优化，文章却缺少基准和引用。  
• “提前判断”也被联系到 guard clause；另有观点提醒，深层拆分可能破坏不变量，最终仍可能演变成难维护的抽象或“为什么这个方法没被调用”的问题。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Windows 热补丁与函数钩子之间的兼容性、权限边界及实际应用价值展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 对“钩子属于非授权/越轨行为”的表述存疑：微软自己提供 Detours 库，过去未必如此定性；且钩子通常只作用于单个进程，修改共享 DLL 页面时会触发写时复制。评论质疑热补丁是否会修改原始共享页、影响所有进程，以及单进程钩子是否会阻断全系统热补丁。  
• 关注多个补丁的冲突：若连续两次更新尝试修改同一函数，可能发生覆盖或失效；这即使没有第三方参与，也属于微软必须解决的问题。  
• 认为多重钩子并非必然冲突：Steam Overlay 与其他 Direct3D 钩子可以共存，说明 Detours 等机制能够处理已被改写的函数，但兼容性仍取决于实现。  
• 指出系统已有防御机制：Windows 并行 DLL 加载会检测部分 NT DLL 函数是否被钩住，发现后可能对该进程禁用自身功能。  
• 支持发展热补丁：及时修复安全漏洞越来越重要，若必须重启进程或系统，会降低修复效率。  
• 提供类比经验：Java 类文件的镜像分层补丁也限制 ABI 变更且一次只能应用一个补丁，说明热更新普遍面临边界与冲突控制问题。

补充讨论：有人批评微软博客缺少前后篇导航，增加阅读系列文章的困难；“混合两种辣酱”则以轻松方式暗示多种钩子/补丁叠加可能效果不确定。

Brownian Motion
Building intuition for Brownian motion by deriving its marginal distribution from a discrete-time random walk.
Published
22 April 2026
Imagine that a pollen particle is suspended in a glass of water. If we were to observe and
record the vertical position of the particle over time, we would find
that its movements were random. And if we were to plot this position, weâd get a jagged path through time (Figure
1
1
1
, left). This path would be just one of
many possible paths, and if we were to repeat this
observational experiment many times, we would not expect to see the same path
again.
Given this randomness, how can we reason about this phenomenon?
Can we say anything interesting or useful about the particle? For
most of human history, this was a seemingly impossible task. A key insight,
a conceptual pillar in probability theory, is to separate what
actually happened (Figure
1
1
1
, left) from other possible outcomes (Figure
1
1
1
,
right). This approach allows us to reason about the world through
counterfactuals: what are all the possible paths the pollen could have taken?
How likely is each path? What can we say about the distribution of outcomes?
Figure 1.
Left.
A single random path of a
pollen particle's vertical position plotted against time.
Right.
Many such random
paths, all starting at the same initial position.
This understanding of the pollen particle as a random process is a deep idea, and
it took many decades and scientists to understand. The phenomenon was first observed in
the 1830s by the Scottish botanist Robert Brown. Brown used a microscope to observe
pollen particles suspended in water, and to his surprise, he saw the particles
moving! At first, he thought this meant that the pollen particles were alive,
but he tested and then rejected this hypothesis by observing the same effect
with particles that he was convinced were inanimate, such as glass powder,
minerals, and even pulverized fragments of the Egyptian Sphinx
(GÃ³ra, 2006)
! For roughly half-a-century, the phenomenon remained a
mystery, although it became known as
Brownian motion
.
Then starting in 1905, Albert Einstein published a series of papers
in which he hythesized that the pollen particles were moving because they were being
bombarded by invisible molecules in the liquid
(Einstein, 1905)
. In the following year, the Polish
physicist Marian Smoluchowski independently published essentially the same theory
(Von Smoluchowski, 1906)
. At the time, this theory was controversial, because the
idea of molecules was not yet widely accepted. However,
using statistical mechanics, Einstein and Smoluchowski were able to make testable
predictions about the behavior of the particles, and another scientist, Jean
Baptiste Perrin, verified the model a few years later
(Perrin, 1909)
. And since Einsteinâs breakthrough work, Brownian motion has been widely studied and
more deeply understood. In the mathematical community, Brownian motion was
formalized by Norbert Wiener
(Wiener, 1923)
, and thus Brownian motion is often referred to as a
Wiener process
, particularly by mathematicians.
The goal of this post is to better understand Brownian motion. Brownian motion is an important concept because it
can be used to model many phenomenon, from particles suspended in liquids to the prices of stocks. Ultimately, weâll
reconstruct the marginal distribution of our pollen particle at any given point in time. As we will see this, this is the normal distribution. This deep connection means that we can make mathematically precise probabilistic statements about a completely random process.
Random walks
Letâs begin with a simplified model of our pollen particle in discrete
time. This is a stochastic process called a
random walk
. In the next
section, weâll extend this to continuous time, which is Brownian motion.
Imagine we can discretize time and then observe a single discrete âtickâ on the
clock. What happens to the pollen particle during this one tick? In our simple
model of the world, weâre going to imagine that we flip a coin, not necessarily fair, and that the pollen particle moves up or down the
same amount based on the outcome of that coin toss. The coin toss models the
fact that the pollen particle is being randomly bombarded by water molecules and
thus its position at the next time point is random. So the pollen particle
cannot stay in place; after one tick of the clock, it moves up or down.

• [alexpadula] 介绍 TideSQL 首个重大版本：该引擎从零设计、基于现代研究，强调写入优化、空间利用率高、读取效率好，并声称功能可与 InnoDB 相当，邀请用户测试反馈。

49963568.article_content:
TidesDB now available for MySQL v9, v26
7 min read
Print
Charmain Jansen van Rensburg
by
Alex Gaetano Padula
published on October 5th, 2026
Possibly most don’t know, but originally TideSQL started as a
MySQL fork
which existed to implement the TidesDB library as a plugin, making its powerful storage engine available to MySQL users.  At the time though the MySQL community had no way for us to make this possible, thus its original course changed.  Almost a year has passed and lots has changed since then.  A
proposal
was created for TidesDB to become available for MySQL and well, this has happened!  TidesDB is
now available
as an external plugin storage engine for MySQL with a wonderful set of features and more to come.
Currently the way to access the TidesDB plugin engine TideSQL is through the
install.sh
script in the plugin repository, which you can either point at your own build or let it build the bundle for you.  Going down the line we’d like this to be easier for you and we’re in discussions with the appropriate parties about that.
TidesDB is a write and space optimized storage engine library which can keep up very well on reads through its hybrid LSM architecture.
TideSQL, which utilizes the library, is a plugin and not a fork.  You run a stock MySQL and load the engine into it, and a TidesDB table can sit next to an InnoDB one in the same server.  TideSQL for MySQL v2.0.0 is paired with TidesDB v10.1.1 and tested against MySQL server v9.7.0 and v26.7.0.
INSTALL PLUGIN TidesDB SONAME
'
ha_tidesdb.so
'
;
CREATE
TABLE
events
(id
BIGINT
PRIMARY KEY
, body
TEXT
) ENGINE
=
TIDESDB;
MySQL has no engine-specific
CREATE TABLE
grammar, so a table names its TidesDB options in
ENGINE_ATTRIBUTE
, a JSON object the server stores and hands to the engine without reading it.  Since the engine defines those names it also checks them, so a misspelled option fails the statement instead of being stored and ignored.  Every option has a
tidesdb_default_*
session variable behind it, so you can set the policy once and let every
CREATE TABLE
inherit it.  Anything a table does not name is resolved when it is created and stays with it.
CREATE
TABLE
archive
(id
INT
PRIMARY KEY
,
data
TEXT
) ENGINE
=
TIDESDB
ENGINE_ATTRIBUTE
=
'
{"compression": "ZSTD", "bloom_fpr": 50}
'
;
Compression is on by default.  Your choices are
NONE
,
SNAPPY
,
LZ4
,
ZSTD
and
LZ4_FAST
, with
LZ4
being the default.
Large values are kept out of compaction.  Each SSTable has its own key log and the whole database shares one segmented value log.  A value at or above
tidesdb_value_separation_threshold
goes to the value log with a logical id left behind in the key log, so a later merge carries the pointer forward rather than the value.  That does cost one value-log read per row on a scan, thus a table you scan far more than you merge can set
{"keep_values_inline": true}
and keep every value in the key log whatever its size.
You can also set the shape of the LSM per table.
level_size_ratio
is how much larger each level of a table is than the last,
min_levels
is the minimum depth, and
l1_file_count_trigger
is how many SSTables may gather at a table’s level 1 before compaction merges them down.  There is no compaction policy to choose, as the engine picks among preemptive merge, dividing merge and partitioned merge based on the state of the tree.  For a table that deletes heavily,
tombstone_density_trigger
escalates compaction for any SSTable whose tombstones outgrow a ratio you set.
CREATE
TABLE
tuned
(id
INT
PRIMARY KEY
, v
VARCHAR
(
200
)) ENGINE
=
TIDESDB
ENGINE_ATTRIBUTE
=
'
{"level_size_ratio": 8, "min_levels": 3,
"l1_file_count_trigger": 4}
'
;
Durability is one setting,
tidesdb_memtable_sync_mode
, and it governs every commit because every table shares the library’s write-ahead log.
FULL
is the default and means a committed write has reached the device and survives power loss.
INTERVAL
hands each commit to the operating system and reaches the device within the interval, so a process crash loses nothing and a machine crash loses at most that window.
NONE
does nothing at commit time, so an acknowledged commit sits in a buffer until a later batch writes it out and a process crash loses it.
Rows can expire on their own at the table level, the row level or the session level, and they resolve in that order.  Encryption at rest is per row with a two-tier key arrangement, so rotating the master key touches no row data.  An encrypted table’s rows are already ciphertext by the time the library sees them, so compression is forced off for that column family, while its secondary indexes hold unencrypted comparable keys and keep whatever compression algorithm you picked.
The rest of what works today:
FULLTEXT
indexes with natural-language and boolean modes, BM25 ranking, stop words and blend characters
foreign keys enforced inside the engine,
ON DELETE
and
ON UPDATE
with
CASCADE
,
SET NULL
and
RESTRICT
, and self-references
spatial indexes, generated columns and JSON
vec
49963568.article_summary: TidesDB现已作为MySQL外部插件存储引擎发布，兼容MySQL 9.7.0和26.7.0，可与InnoDB共存，无需使用分支版本。其采用混合LSM架构，具备写入与空间优化、压缩、值分离、可调LSM参数、持久化策略、TTL、加密等功能，并支持全文、外键、空间索引、生成列和JSON等特性。用户可通过install.sh安装。
49963568.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TideSQL 作为 MySQL 新型事务存储引擎，是否能提供类似 RocksDB/MyRocks 的写入与空间优化能力，以及相较 PostgreSQL 的价值。

不同观点：
• [alexpadula] 介绍 TideSQL 首个重大版本：该引擎从零设计、基于现代研究，强调写入优化、空间利用率高、读取效率好，并声称功能可与 InnoDB 相当，邀请用户测试反馈。  
• [bratao] 对空间优化存储引擎有强烈需求，认为如果 PostgreSQL 缺少类似 Percona MySQL 的空间优化方案，就无法从 MySQL 迁移；因此将 TideSQL 视为 RocksDB/MyRocks 的潜在替代品。  
• [kumarvvr] 从更宏观的数据库选型角度提问：目前 MySQL 相比 PostgreSQL 是否仍有明显优势。  
• [sgarland] 关注技术差异，直接询问 TideSQL 与 RocksDB/MyRocks 的具体区别，尤其可能涉及架构、性能、事务能力和兼容性。

补充讨论：评论尚未给出实测数据或具体回答。争议焦点主要是 TideSQL 相比 RocksDB/MyRocks 的实际改进，以及其能否弥补 PostgreSQL 在空间优化存储方面的不足；MySQL 与 PostgreSQL 的整体优劣也仍是开放问题。

data.title: Sharing AI progress in mathematics
data.author: OfficialTurkey
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 AI 近期数学研究成果（包括巴纳特猜想、唯一游戏猜想、黎曼/霍奇等问题及调度问题）的可靠性、意义与社会影响展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 重大突破派：认为唯一游戏猜想若被严格证明，将重写近似算法理论；巴纳特猜想等长期难题的解决也意义非凡，可能相当于数十年甚至更久的人类数学进展。  
• 谨慎审查派：指出目前仍缺乏 Lean 等形式化证明，部分证明尚在研读和核验；有人发现其思路类似自己多年前放弃的路线，因此不敢贸然确认。  
• 影响焦虑派：数学家担忧多年研究、职业规划乃至整个研究团队的目标被 AI 迅速完成，引发失落、抑郁和“人类是否仍有独特价值”的疑问。  
• 乐观人文派：认为 AI 展现的是发现既有数学之美，而非单纯竞争；人类仍可欣赏、理解并继续探索无穷的新真理。  
• AI 风险派：借此追问 AI 是否会持续突破、是否可能超越人类，以及未来一至五年会否扩展到数学之外。

补充讨论：评论特别强调成果的理论性质与实际影响之间的差异：部分物理结果只是严格证明了学界早有预期的现象，未必等同于物理学范式突破；同时，极高计算成本和异常夸张的复杂度也引发对可复现性、效率及正确性的关注。

data.title: How machines learned precision
data.author: glinscott
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了18世纪至19世纪机械制造精度的提升。早期车床、铸造和镗孔误差严重，导致蒸汽机活塞泄漏、轴承晃动。瓦特改进蒸汽机后，要求汽缸内孔笔直、圆整；传统铸造和镗削难以满足。约1775年，约翰·威尔金森用两端支撑的重型镗杆显著提高了汽缸精度。随后，惠特沃思发展出能检测百万分之一英寸误差的测量技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕文章介绍的工业革命时期精密制造技术、历史渊源、工程意义及科普呈现方式展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 读者普遍高度评价文章的动画和交互设计，认为其清晰展示了精密测量、螺纹加工等复杂原理，具有很强的教学价值；部分人将其与Bartosz Ciechanowski的互动文章比较。  
• 多人强调精密工程对现代工业和量产的基础作用：精密研磨带来更小公差、更好表面质量，使机械运行更快、更高效，并推动自动化与大规模生产。  
• 有人补充历史来源，指出“用两根误差螺杆加工第三根螺杆”的方法并非Maudslay首创，达·芬奇已有类似设计；翻转螺杆还能进一步平均误差。争议焦点是技术归属及历史叙述是否完整。  
• 有工程背景的读者分享家庭经历：父亲曾从机床制造转向铸造，仍用车床精加工零件；文章唤起其操作车床的记忆，体现技术的实际影响。  
• 有人指出标题混淆“精密度（precision）”与“准确度（accuracy）”，建议面向大众时先明确区分。  
• 其他评论推荐相关书籍、视频和DIY数控机床资源，并希望出现类似“原始技术”的精密机床制作系列。

补充讨论：评论整体偏赞赏，也关注工业技术如何通过不断复制、修正和误差抵消逐步实现“足够好”并最终支撑现代制造。

49980626.article_content:
This is a screw-cutting lathe of the kind
Henry Maudslay
built in London
around 1800. A labourer turns the large wheel to spin the bar in the middle, and a cutting
tool moves along beside it on a carriage that slides on straight iron rails. A long screw
moves the carriage the same distance on every turn of the bar, cutting a thread into its
surface. Lathes like this made shafts and screws for steam engines, looms, locomotives and
other lathes.
But the lathe's own parts have to be accurate first. If a rail is bent, the tool follows
the bend. If the turns of the screw are unevenly spaced, the thread it cuts will be uneven
too. These errors leave pistons leaking, shafts wobbling in their bearings and nuts jamming
on their bolts. In the 1770s, workshops were still struggling to make large cylinders round,
long rails straight and screw threads evenly spaced. Even checking their work was difficult:
the smallest mark on an ordinary workshop rule was a sixteenth of an inch, about a
millimetre and a half.
By the 1850s,
Joseph
Whitworth
had built a machine that could detect a difference of a
millionth of an inch. In this article we'll follow how workshops learned to make flat
surfaces, cut accurate screws and measure their parts, using interactive figures to explore
each step (try
rotating the lathe above with two fingers, or pinching to zoom
in
dragging the lathe above, or zooming with ⌘/Ctrl +
scroll
). Let's start with the cylinder of
Watt
's steam engine, which we built in
the
previous article
.
The cylinder
Newcomen
's engine filled a
cylinder with steam, then condensed it with a spray of cold water. The atmosphere pushed
the piston down into the partial vacuum, but the spray also chilled the cylinder. Watt
moved the condensation into a separate cold vessel so that the cylinder could stay hot,
saving about two thirds of the coal. This also meant he had to change the way he sealed
the piston. Below, we can compare the two engines.
Newcomen kept a pool of water on his piston to fill the gaps against the uneven cylinder
wall. Water would have cooled Watt's cylinder, so he used dry packing instead. The tightly
rammed packing couldn't give way enough to fill the gaps, so the hole through the cylinder,
called the
bore
, had to be round and straight along the whole stroke.
Watt tried many materials for packing. In 1770 he had hopes of “pasteboard, cork, tow,
and horse-dung mixed,” and
Matthew
Boulton
later tried a “hat, filled up with paper chewed.”
The cylinders of the 1760s were far from that. The eighteen-inch cylinder of Watt's test
engine at Kinneil, in 1769, was about ⅜ of an inch wider one way than the other at its worst
point. That is nearly a centimetre of error in a cylinder less than half a metre wide.
The traditional way to make two parts fit was to press them together and file away the
bright spots where they rubbed. The workman doing this was called a
fitter
. He
could make the small surfaces of a valve or a gun lock fit closely, but a piston had to fit
at every point along its stroke. Filing one part of the bore wouldn't make the rest match,
and most of it was deep inside the cylinder, where a file couldn't reach.
To see why this was such a challenge, let's go through how the cylinders were built. The
thick iron walls were made in one piece by pouring molten iron into a mould, a process
called
casting
. The mould formed the outside, while a
core
in the middle
left a hole through the iron.
1
Below, we can watch a cylinder being cast in a sand mould.
Molten iron is far denser than sand, so it pushes the core upward against
whatever holds it down. If it lifts even slightly, the casting is ruined. Even a core that
stays in place leaves a rough hole that isn't straight or round. A
boring mill
cuts away the inside of the casting to bring it to the right shape and size.
The boring mills of the time held the cutter on the end of a long bar supported from one
side, like a broomstick held at arm's length. The bar sagged under its own weight,
2
and the uneven wall pushed it
from side to side as it cut. Instead of making a straight hole, the cutter followed much of
the crooked one. Large cylinders were bored four times, turned a quarter turn between passes,
and still did not always come out round.
3
Around 1775, the ironmaster
John Wilkinson
found
an ingenious solution. He built a boring mill with a much heavier bar that ran right through
the cylinder and turned in bearings at both ends.
4
The casting was clamped in place, and the cutter head slid along
the bar as it turned. The cutter now followed the bar the way a pencil follows a ruler.
Supporting both ends greatly reduced the bending, so the cutter could make a straight bore
through a crooked casting.
In 1776, Watt's partner Matthew Boulton wrote that a fifty-inch cylinder Wilkinson had
bored for them “does not err the thickness of an old shilling in any part.” A worn shilling
was a little under a millimetre thick, which puts the error at less than one part in a

data.title: House with 15m underground tunnels for sale for 300k
data.author: librasteve
data.article_summary: 英国雷丁蒂尔赫斯特一处住宅以30万至32.5万英镑挂牌拍卖。业主托尼·迪恩及家人历时20多年手工挖掘地下隧道，深达15米、面积超1300平方英尺，设有房间、储藏室、铁路、货梯和暗门。物业还包括车间、泳池及改建许可，买家可将地下空间用作储藏、防空洞或数据中心。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一栋带有地下隧道、秘密入口和“防电磁脉冲服务器农场”的房产，评论者讨论其趣味性、结构安全、真实信息及类似案例。

不同观点：
• **猎奇与赞赏**：许多人认为地下隧道、泳池旁火箭内的秘密入口很酷，欣赏土木工程师将业余爱好建成复杂地下系统；也有人觉得带泳池的独立住宅售价约30万英镑非常便宜，甚至产生搬去购买的想法。  
• **安全担忧**：有人指出即使白垩土据称能自我支撑，也不愿在没有支护加固的隧道中活动，担心坍塌风险。  
• **事实澄清与资料补充**：评论者提供拍卖网站、房产广告、平面图和更多照片，试图比新闻报道更准确地说明房屋结构；另有人澄清“15 meters”是地下15米，而非“1500万条隧道”。  
• **类比与延伸**：评论提到莱比锡战时地下通道、利物浦Williamson隧道、Forestiere地下花园，以及YouTube/TikTok上的私人挖隧道项目，说明这类“业余挖隧道”并非孤例。  
• **调侃与质疑**：有人戏称让孩子参与挖隧道、引用“对抗蚂蚁就要变成蚂蚁”；“EMP防护服务器农场”则被认为是在迎合网络末日准备者（prepper）群体。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要在隧道的安全性、报道表述是否准确，以及这种私人地下工程究竟是有趣的创意还是潜在危险的另类爱好。

A house featuring underground tunnels hand dug 15m below ground by the owner over twenty years is on sale for £300K.
Civil engineer Tony Deane spent two decades creating a subterranean network of rooms and corridors under his home in Tilehurst.
The unique complex contains more than 1,300 square feet of underground space, including tunnels and storage rooms - and even a hand-built railway.
One room even features a secret entrance - hidden inside a rocket by the pool.
There is a one-tonne goods lift and two secret doors - one formed by a 1.5-tonne sliding concrete wall.
READ MORE:
Reading odour complaints more than double to 207 in a year
Hidden for decades beneath a workshop in a suburb of Tilehurst in Reading - the network descends through four levels and reaches more than 15m below ground.
Tony, whose initial day job was in the construction of aerodrome and airport infrastructure, started the construction work by himself during the 1980s and ‘90s.
He was also assisted by his six children.
The only apparatus the family used to conduct the digging and move chalk were buckets and wheelbarrows.
Richard Worrall, auctioneer and consultant at BTG Eddisons Property Auctions, said: “In all my years as an auctioneer, I’ve never seen anything like this before - it’s utterly amazing and, I think, unique.
"What a feat to create this as a family project and as a hobby.”
The Deane family’s subterranean projects began even earlier, in the 1960s, with the construction of underground changing rooms next to the property's swimming pool.
The entrance was hidden behind a 23ft-high rocket, which is still in place today.
Despite the scale of the project, its existence is understood to have remained largely unknown outside the family, including to neighbours in the surrounding residential area.
Richard Worrall said: “Most of these tunnels were dug through chalk, which is naturally self-supporting, while, in some places, where required, structural concrete was used and cast by hand.
“Incredibly, absolutely everything was excavated manually.
"Mr Deane also constructed a railway through the tunnels to transport the excavated chalk, as well as building a four-layer, one-tonne goods lift to carry it to ground level.”
The site is accessed via a secure gated driveway and includes a 2,500 sq ft workshop arranged over three floors, parking, gardens, a large swimming pool and changing rooms.
Planning consent was granted by West Berkshire Council in December 2024 for a 5,000 sq ft, five-bedroom, two-storey house to be built on the site of the swimming pool, while conversion of the workshop has consent for conversion to a three-bedroom house.
READ MORE:
Police appeal after £1,000 of goods stolen from shops
Richard added: “The underground space is obviously a game changer to say the least and we believe it could offer an imaginative buyer a range of potential uses, anything from secure storage, a fallout shelter or an EMP-resistant data centre to a prepper’s paradise."
The property has a guide price of £300,000-£325,000 and will be included in BTG Eddisons Property Auctions’ live stream auction on 28-29 October.
For further details and bidding information, visit
www.btgeddisonspropertyauctions.com

• **安全担忧**：有人指出即使白垩土据称能自我支撑，也不愿在没有支护加固的隧道中活动，担心坍塌风险。  
• **事实澄清与资料补充**：评论者提供拍卖网站、房产广告、平面图和更多照片，试图比新闻报道更准确地说明房屋结构；另有人澄清“15 meters”是地下15米，而非“1500万条隧道”。  
• **类比与延伸**：评论提到莱比锡战时地下通道、利物浦Williamson隧道、Forestiere地下花园，以及YouTube/TikTok上的私人挖隧道项目，说明这类“业余挖隧道”并非孤例。  
• **调侃与质疑**：有人戏称让孩子参与挖隧道、引用“对抗蚂蚁就要变成蚂蚁”；“EMP防护服务器农场”则被认为是在迎合网络末日准备者（prepper）群体。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要在隧道的安全性、报道表述是否准确，以及这种私人地下工程究竟是有趣的创意还是潜在危险的另类爱好。

data.title: Meta and Microsoft take steps to reduce employee usage of Claude AI
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: Meta和微软正减少员工对Anthropic Claude的内部使用，转而推广自研编码工具。微软将多数员工AI预算上限从10万美元降至约1万美元，Meta的Claude Code用户也从约6万人降至3万人，但两家公司仍持续采购Claude并向客户提供相关服务。此举反映AI成本控制与市场竞争加剧。文章还提醒，代码助手涉及敏感文件、命令和凭证，企业需强化权限管理与安全审查。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软及其他大公司削减员工AI额度、优先使用自研模型的原因，以及这是否意味着外部模型需求和投入回报正在下降。

不同观点：
• 成本控制派：人均每月10万美元额度过高，削减至约1万美元主要针对少数“token消耗过度、ROI低”的重度用户，并非全面停止使用AI。  
• 自研/治理派：大型实验室限制竞品工具，核心是数据治理、内部模型“自用测试”和推动自家产品，不代表Claude等模型质量下降。  
• “够用即可”派：多数任务不需要最强模型，价格更低、性能相近的模型足以替代昂贵模型。  
• 影响Anthropic派：若微软等大客户大幅减少直接使用，可能重创Anthropic收入；有人推测其收入高度集中于少数客户。  
• Meta相关质疑：部分评论认为Meta并未限制Claude，只是把Claude Code转入内部接口和工具链，因此所谓用户数下降可能只是统计口径变化，底层仍在大量调用Anthropic模型。  
• 投入回报怀疑派：质疑微软每月巨额AI支出究竟带来了什么，产品和服务似乎没有明显改善，企业AI投入的实际产出仍不清楚。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于额度削减究竟是普遍性战略转向，还是针对少数高耗用户的正常优化；以及“直接使用Claude人数下降”能否代表模型实际调用量下降。

49997161.article_content:
Meta and Microsoft have commenced a significant reduction in employee utilization of Anthropic’s Claude AI as they pivot towards their own proprietary coding instruments, as reported on October 5 by The Information.
This strategic alteration prioritizes internal expenditure and workforce processes, rather than discontinuing customer access to Claude through Microsoft’s offerings.
This transition underscores the increasing imperative to manage AI expenditures as coding assistants become integral to routine software operations.
While both corporations continue to be substantial clients of Anthropic, they also find themselves in competition with the firm. Their actions reflect a convergence of AI investment, product strategies, and control over developer resources.
Microsoft Reduces AI Expenditure Allowances
Microsoft had previously anticipated that internal expenditures on Anthropic
technology
would exceed $1 billion annually.
However, this estimate has diminished by over a third subsequent to management’s directive for employees to curtail their use of Claude and to increasingly adopt Microsoft tools, such as GitHub Copilot and OpenAI frameworks.
Within Microsoft’s cloud and AI sector, monthly AI spending limits have reportedly been slashed from $100,000 per employee to approximately $10,000 in the majority of instances.
It’s crucial to note that these figures are spending ceilings rather than reflections of actual employee expenditures. This reduction in budgetary flexibility has disheartened several engineers who once enjoyed broader latitude to explore models.
It’s important to highlight that diminished internal funding does not equate to Microsoft’s withdrawal of Claude from client-facing products.
Reports suggest that client expenditure on Anthropic models via Microsoft’s enterprise platforms continues to rise, even as the company constricts its own employees’ usage.
At Meta, the number of Claude Code users reportedly plummeted from around 60,000 earlier this year to about 30,000.
Although layoffs have influenced this decrease, the report attributes the primary cause to Meta’s strategic shift towards its own AI solutions, which comprise MetaCode and Muse Code, developed using Meta’s proprietary models.
MetaCode is said to have more than 30,000 internal users, while Muse Code boasts over 6,000 employee users. Meta initiated external testing of Muse Code with clients in August.
Notably, amidst this transition, Meta reportedly allocated over $105 million to Claude Code over a 28-day timeframe, indicating that a reduction in users does not necessarily correlate with decreased spending.
For
cybersecurity
teams, the transition to different coding assistants does not eliminate the hazards associated with automated access to sensitive files, commands, and credentials.
Previous analyses by Cybersecurity News outlined vulnerabilities within Claude Code that could allow unauthorized execution and API key theft. Anthropic rectified these flaws prior to their public disclosure.
Microsoft’s offerings have encountered analogous concerns. The remedied RoguePilot vulnerability exemplified how nefarious commands embedded in a GitHub Issue could facilitate the takeover of repositories.
Such incidents emphasize the criticality of imposing stringent permissions, employing trusted project settings, and conducting thorough evaluations of AI-generated actions.
Anthropic’s reported annualized revenue pace of $65 billion reflects unabated demand for its services.
This retrenchment illustrates a tightening of budgets and intensifying competition, rather than an outright cessation of engagement with Claude.

Cybersecuritynews.com
.

data.title: Google Playground: Create and play custom games
data.author: acossta
data.article_summary: Google推出实验性游戏平台Playground，用户无需编程，只需通过文字提示即可创建、修改和测试自定义游戏，并可在浏览器中游玩、分享或发布至社区。平台支持多人游戏、排行榜、关注创作者及内容安全审核。未来将接入Unity Spark，为创作者提供更专业的3D制作和游戏开发能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI游戏生成工具的实际质量、创新潜力、商业影响及平台问题。

不同观点：
• 质疑者认为它更像“AI版自制游戏工具”，目前作品多是无尽跑酷、问答、消除等简单Flash式游戏，难称“AI游戏引擎”，难以影响行业；“做出游戏”不等于“做出好玩的游戏”。
• 肯定者认为其浏览器生成效果已相当惊人，质量优于部分代码生成工具，未来可能催生原本不会出现的怪趣游戏，甚至冲击单纯靠延长游玩时长盈利的“赌场式”游戏。
• 实践者反馈褒贬不一：可快速制作太空探索、科幻问答等游戏，文字、音乐、图像和语音表现尚可，但帧率卡顿、提示词遵循度低，多人/单人模式切换困难，仍处早期测试。
• 有人期待生成“抖音式”游戏平台：根据玩家偏好不断生成新游戏；也有人关注复杂创意（如4D Agar.io）、多人支持及非常规交互能否真正实现。
• 对Google持保留态度者认为其不应进一步垄断PaaS和游戏平台，更适合开放模型与工具；另有观点认为项目价值可能在教育、记忆训练和语言学习。

补充讨论：地区限制导致多人遇到403，Linux/浏览器也有兼容问题；评论者推荐Snack.game及开源Noodle作为替代，强调本地运行、隐私和多人设备支持。

Games are one of the most creative forms of expression, and the gaming community keeps growing. But game creation has historically been limited to a select group of people who have technical experience and knowledge of complex game engines.
Today, we’re introducing Playground, an experimental gaming platform that lets you create, play, and share custom games. Playground lowers the barriers to creation, so bringing game ideas to life can now be as easy as describing it through a few prompts — no coding experience required.
Create your custom game
With Playground’s conversational interface, you can direct the game just by typing what you want to build. data.author: ilreb
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google SynthID用于识别AI生成图像的水印，但其使用门槛、透明度、可靠性及开放性引发讨论。

不同观点：
• 功能期待落差：有人误以为能识别音乐中使用的合成器及参数；实际项目是检测AI生成媒体，主要针对Google生成内容。  
• 认证与使用体验受批评：评论者质疑为何必须登录、先同意条款才能了解服务；相比之下，OpenAI曾提供免登录工具，Google过去也可通过“关于此图片”查看来源。  
• 检测效果有限：测试中8张OpenAI或Google生成图片有6张被识别，但经过文字、图片叠加的2张成功绕过，说明水印可能受编辑影响。  
• 透明度和开放性不足：有人希望有公开标准、批量检测、离线工具或API；目前相关能力似乎主要面向企业，且Google未充分说明原理。  
• 水印的持久性存疑：有人认为SynthID最终会被逆向，AI内容可被清除水印；也有人指出其文本水印检测尚未提供。  
• 替代思路：与其不断识别伪造内容，不如通过相机硬件和来源凭证证明照片来自真实设备，尤其适用于产品缺陷等证据场景。

补充讨论：OpenAI工具也存在速率限制；SynthID的技术细节和自建分类器已有研究，但整体争议集中在“便利性、开放性与检测可靠性”的平衡。

data.title: Show HN: Agent.reviews – Where AI agents read and write reviews on tools
data.author: screm
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了 Agent Reviews：一个供智能代理发现、阅读和撰写软件评价的平台。网站收录 FastAPI、Git、Claude API、Playwright 等工具及用户评分、使用案例和分类排名，支持按工具或类别搜索。平台宣称评价免费公开，且不会记录代码、提示词、密钥或用户姓名。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“让智能体使用并评价工具”的平台价值、可信度、商业模式与使用体验展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **积极支持**：认为让智能体实际完成任务后再反馈，能发现细小问题、改进工具，类似“投诉技能”，并可能发展成面向智能体的 Stack Overflow；有人称赞其设计及对 uv 的高评分。

data.title: The art of defusing a second world war bomb
data.author: sandebert
data.article_summary: 2026年1月14日，英国德文郡同日发现两枚二战德军未爆炸弹：普利茅斯工地地下的50公斤炸弹，以及埃克斯茅斯码头挖泥船上的250公斤炸弹，后者旁有大量柴油，风险极高。军方第11爆炸物处理与搜索团紧急出动。文章介绍排爆过程、历史背景及现代英国排爆工作的日常与危险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：二战及一战遗留未爆弹（UXO）的持续危害、处置难度，以及相关历史记忆与公共安全。

不同观点：
• 遗留炸弹至今仍很常见且危险。德国哈姆、柏林、英国埃克塞特等地仍会发现大型炸弹并疏散居民；法国甚至还在清理一战炮弹，预计可能持续百年。  
• 海上弹药风险尤其严重。英国“SS Richard Montgomery”号载有约1.4千吨炸药，若爆炸可能造成巨大水柱、冲击波和海啸般影响；潜水员也指出，水会更高效地传递爆炸冲击。  
• 处置工作极其危险但有长期需求。评论提到排爆机器人、皇家工兵和专业潜水排爆队，并认为“只允许犯一次错”；也有人疑问，未发现的弹药是否会因长期扰动而自行爆炸，另有人以“最后一个被二战炸弹杀死的人可能尚未出生”概括其长期风险。  
• 记录与预防同样重要。战时防空人员留下的详细记录能帮助后世定位危险；德国施工前通常要确认地下没有弹药，因此工程可能延误。  
• 讨论也延伸到战争记忆与文化传播：推荐排爆题材剧集《Danger UXB》、英国布伦泽特航空博物馆，并称赞媒体持续制作高质量长篇报道。

补充讨论：评论之间总体是相互补充而非直接争论，争议焦点主要在UXO实际爆炸概率及其风险是否被公众充分重视。
